title: Chemical Attack on Barrier Layers
introduction: Chemical agents present in the PV module environment — particularly acetic acid released by thermally or photochemically degrading EVA encapsulant — attack metallic barrier layers within the module structure. This chemical stressor does not impose direct mechanical loads but instead weakens structural integrity through corrosion, creating micro-cracks that compromise the barrier function of aluminum-containing layers in backsheet constructions. Acetic acid is the initial product of EVA degradation and is linked to several PV module failure mechanisms through its corrosive action on metals.
reasoning: The 657-Elsevier study documents acetic acid from EVA degradation corroding aluminum barrier layers in PV backsheets, creating micro-cracks that enhance acid transport — a distinct crack-initiating chemical stressor.

key_findings.claim: Acetic acid formed during EVA degradation is linked to multiple PV module failure mechanisms including corrosion of aluminum-containing barriers
key_findings.detail: Acetic acid is formed during degradation of EVA, the most frequently used PV encapsulant, and is linked to several module failure mechanisms. [^elsevier657a] The initial step of EVA degradation is the formation of this acetic acid, which then accumulates in the module interior where it attacks metal components. [^elsevier657b]

source_locations.quote: Acetic acid, which is formed during degradation of the most frequently used photovoltaic (PV) encapsulant ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA), is linked to several PV module failure mechanisms
The initial step of EVA degradation is the formation of acetic acid

key_findings.claim: Acetic acid corrosion of aluminum barrier layers creates pinholes and micro-cracks confirmed by REM-EDX and FTIR-ATR spectroscopy
key_findings.detail: Corrosion of the aluminum barrier layer in PV backsheets by acetic acid has been verified by REM-EDX and FTIR-ATR spectroscopy. The corrosion creates pinholes and micro-cracks in the aluminum layer. [^elsevier657c] The corrosion process also produces aluminum acetate and small crystal formations, along with increased surface porosity and small holes. [^elsevier657d]

source_locations.quote: Corrosion of the aluminium layer has been shown with REM-EDX and FTIR-ATR spectroscopy, creating pinholes or micro-cracks
The formation of small crystals ... and the formation of small holes was observed
